A seat begins with a domain. At join the node pulls the RDAP record for a host the applicant controls: creation date past twelve months, no renewal gap, then wants a TXT record binding that domain to the key. One domain holds one seat, rechecked every epoch.

No comet-fast trick skips the age. Aftermarket names run 60 to 200 dollars, so fifty clones cost 3,000 to 10,000 dollars plus renewals, and a juniper-fresh domain registered yesterday fails the birth date no matter how good the site looks.

An onyx bands over geologic time; a domain is only as old as its registry says.
